lines.caption: This is a tour of the pull request for issue 135: Enter in the search box now jumps to the results.
lines.say: This is a tour of the pull request for issue one thirty-five: Enter in the search box now jumps to the results.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
Enter in the search box now moves the focus to the results, and the search stays as it is.
You press Ctrl+F and type a word, and the results update as you type.
lines.say: You press Control F and type a word, and the results update as you type.

lines.caption: When you press Enter, the box sees that its text is a search, and takes a new branch.
That branch first disarms a handler, so the location bar stays a search when the focus leaves it.
Then it moves the keyboard focus to the file list.
Down now selects the first match, using the list's own keys, and the search stays on screen.
Enter on a folder or file path still works exactly as before.
Before, Enter did nothing in the search box, and you needed Tab twice to reach the results.
Search runs on every keystroke, so Enter's only new job is moving the keyboard to the results.
Without the disarm step, the path-buttons bar would swap back to buttons in the middle of a search.
The focus call is the same one the location bar already makes after selecting a file, from issue 93.
lines.say: The focus call is the same one the location bar already makes after selecting a file, from issue ninety-three.

lines.caption: The whole change is this one new branch in the Enter handler.
One thing differs from the issue: Ctrl+F during a search turns it off, so it doesn't take you back. Clicking does.
lines.say: One thing differs from the issue: Control F during a search turns it off, so it doesn't take you back. Clicking does.

lines.caption: The PR changes one source file and adds a verify script and this page.
To undo it, revert the PR. Nothing else depends on it.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was tested by a new verify script in the cloud container and reviewed locally. CI has not run yet.
lines.say: It was tested by a new verify script in the cloud container and reviewed locally. C I has not run yet.

lines.caption: It reuses an existing focus call, and the issue had already shown the list's Down key works in search results.
The debs were built and installed, and all 29 verify tests passed, both before and after the review fix.
lines.say: The debs were built and installed, and all twenty-nine verify tests passed, both before and after the review fix.

lines.caption: The new script checked that Enter, then Down, selects exactly apple1.txt.
lines.say: The new script checked that Enter, then Down, selects exactly apple one dot t x t.

lines.caption: It checked that the search stays after Enter, with both bar styles.
And with no matches, Enter and Down leave Thunar running.
Ctrl+F after Enter was read in the code, not tested: it turns the search off.
lines.say: Control F after Enter was read in the code, not tested: it turns the search off.

lines.caption: CI, its screenshot audit and the narrated video have not run yet.
lines.say: C I, its screenshot audit and the narrated video have not run yet.

lines.caption: A local review before the first push found three things.
One was a real bug with the path-buttons bar. It was fixed, and the script tests that layout.
A missing check was skipped as a nit, and the missing explainer is this page.
Your installed Thunar gets the change with the next package built from main.
Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue depends on this one. What is left is your call on Ctrl+F.
lines.say: No open issue depends on this one. What is left is your call on Control F.

lines.caption: You decide whether Ctrl+F after Enter keeps toggling the search off, or goes back to the search box.
lines.say: You decide whether Control F after Enter keeps toggling the search off, or goes back to the search box.

lines.caption: Changing it would be its own issue, since it changes the search toggle for everyone.
In short: type a search, press Enter, then Down, and you're on the first match.
